score.note: Score falls in CONDITIONAL AUTHORIZE band (3.0 ≤ 3.05 < 3.5). Wave 2 may proceed only after all conditions are satisfied and with the specified constraints.

criteria_scores.rationale: GovernanceGuardP2 exists as a standalone Node.js module (710 lines, 11 rules) and validates correctly (30/30 PASS, 0 violations). All 11 rules implemented including P2-specific Rule 11 (Part2OnlyFlag). String-aware brace-matcher included (DL-020 prevention). However, it is NOT registered in opencode.json as an OpenCode plugin — the active plugin chain only includes 'governance-guard' (P1). Write-time automatic enforcement is NOT active. The guard can be invoked programmatically before saves, but this requires manual discipline.
criteria_scores.evidence: node -e 'new require("./scripts/governance_guard_p2.js").GovernanceGuardP2().validatePack("pack_p2_a.js")' → PASS, 30 items, 0 violations. opencode.json 'plugin' array → governance-guard (P1 only).

criteria_scores.rationale: All 4 critical structural defect classes have detection rules in the governance guard: DL-008 (Rule 2 — EW[CC] non-empty), DL-026 (Rule 6 — empty non-CC EW slots), DL-021 (Rule 10 — absent EW fields), DL-037 (Rule 9 — Yes/No polarity mismatch). Single-object architecture eliminates DL-016 (metadata-content mismatch) and DL-029 (CC-offset false positives) entirely. Wave 1 produced 30/30 structurally clean items — zero violations across all rules. Authoring quality demonstrates defect-aware construction even without formal templates.
criteria_scores.evidence: GovernanceGuardP2.validatePack('pack_p2_a.js') → 0 violations. P2005 bootstrap audit: 0 DL-008, 0 DL-026, 0 DL-013. All 30 items structurally verified.

criteria_scores.rationale: Wave 1 items are professionally authored with realistic business scenarios, named stakeholders, proper Part 2 authority citations (ASC, COSO ERM, CAPM), choice-specific distractor explanations, and CommonTrapReference on every item. Part2OnlyFlag: true on all 30 items. Zero structural defects. However, P2-A-017 has embedded authoring notes and incomplete calculations in the ExplanationCorrect field — a critical learner-safety issue. The underlying math is correct but the presentation is not production-ready.
criteria_scores.evidence: P2005 bootstrap: 'HIGH QUALITY for a first authoring wave.' 29 of 30 items would pass gates if infrastructure existed. P2-A-017 blocked by drafting notes. CC B-bias: 40% B (target 22-28%).

criteria_scores.rationale: CRITICAL CONCERN: All 30 Wave 1 items are Difficult (70%, 21/30) or Very Difficult (30%, 9/30). All 30 items are Analyze (53%, 16/30) or Evaluate (47%, 14/30). Zero Easy, Moderate-Easy, Moderate difficulty. Zero Remember, Understand, Apply cognitive levels. P2002 §G targets for Domain A: Easy 10%, Mod-Easy 20%, Moderate 30%. Current cumulative: 0%/0%/0%. Domain A Bloom's targets: Remember 10%, Understand 20%, Apply 45%. Current cumulative: 0%/0%/0%. This is a severe distribution skew that Wave 2 MUST correct.
criteria_scores.evidence: P2005 bootstrap structuralMetrics. Difficulty: 0 Easy, 0 Mod-Easy, 0 Moderate, 21 Difficult, 9 Very Difficult. Cognitive: 0 Remember, 0 Understand, 0 Apply, 16 Analyze, 14 Evaluate.

The governance mapping (P2002_GOVERNANCE_MAPPING.json) classifies all 101 elements. The governance bootstrap (P2003_GOVERNANCE_BOOTSTRAP.json) defines all 14 mandatory items. prerequisites.description: Fix P2-A-017 — embedded authoring notes in ExplanationCorrect and VerificationChecks. The ExplanationCorrect contains 'Let me re-derive...', 'Ugh, I made an error...', 'I need to fix...' — exposing internal authoring process to learners. The Choice B text also has contradictory numbers (claims 7.84% margin, then recalculates to 6.73% mid-text).
prerequisites.remediation: Rewrite Choice B and ExplanationCorrect with clean, internally consistent text. Correct margin calculation → 6.73% is the correct normalized NPM. The item's argument (that normalized NPM is BELOW 7.0%) is correct; clean the presentation. Clean VerificationChecks to remove drafting commentary.

prerequisites.description: Define formal Wave 2 authoring protocol. Every item must: (a) pass GovernanceGuardP2.validateItem() before inclusion in the pack file, (b) carry Part2OnlyFlag: true, (c) have ALL 4 ExplanationWrong fields present with CC slot empty and 3 distractor slots ≥50 chars, (d) have a VerificationChecks field listing structural validation results, (e) not exceed the difficulty/cognitive distribution targets defined in PR02.

conditions.condition: Wave 2 MUST produce ≤3 items labeled Difficult (4) and 0 items labeled Very Difficult (5). The cumulative difficulty distribution after Wave 2 must show measurable improvement toward Domain A targets.
conditions.rationale: Wave 1 skewed 100% Difficult+. Wave 2 is the only immediate opportunity to inject lower-tier items. Adding more Difficult items at this stage would compound the distribution problem and make later rebalancing harder.
conditions.verification: After Wave 2: grep '"Difficulty"' on pack_p2_a.js and confirm Easy ≥6, Mod-Easy ≥10, Moderate ≥11, Difficult ≤24, VeryDifficult ≤9.

conditions.condition: Wave 2 MUST produce ≥6 Remember, ≥10 Understand, and ≥11 Apply cognitive-level items. The cumulative cognitive distribution must include all 5 Bloom's levels after Wave 2.
conditions.rationale: Wave 1 skews 100% Analyze/Evaluate. Domain A's Apply target is 45% — the largest single category. Wave 2 must begin populating it. Without Remember/Understand items, the pool lacks foundational knowledge questions.
conditions.verification: After Wave 2: grep '"CognitiveLevel"' on pack_p2_a.js and confirm Remember ≥6, Understand ≥10, Apply ≥11.

conditions.condition: Wave 2 MUST reduce the CorrectChoice B-bias. No more than 3 of the 30 Wave 2 items may have CorrectChoice=B. Target positions A/C/D should each receive 8-10 items to bring all four positions toward 22-28%.
conditions.rationale: Current distribution: A=23%, B=40%, C=20%, D=17%. B occupies 40% while D is at 17% — a 23-point spread. Candidates who notice pattern bias lose confidence in the exam's psychometric validity.
conditions.verification: After Wave 2: all four CorrectChoice positions between 18-32% of 60 items (acceptable interim range; tighten to 22-28% at 500 items).

conditions.condition: Wave 2 items MUST be validated through GovernanceGuardP2.validateItem() BEFORE inclusion in pack_p2_a.js. BLOCKED violations (Rules 2,5,6,9,10,11) → item rejected. WARN violations → documented and acknowledged.
conditions.rationale: Governance guard is not registered as an OpenCode plugin, so write-time enforcement is not automatic. Programmatic validation before saving is the only available enforcement mechanism.
conditions.verification: GovernanceGuardP2.validatePack('pack_p2_a.js') after Wave 2 → 0 BLOCK violations. WARN violations documented in REVISION_HISTORY_P2.md.

conditions.condition: Wave 2 items MUST follow the established Wave 1 item schema: single JSON object per item with Part, Section, Topic, QuestionID, question_state, Part2OnlyFlag, Stem, Choices.{A,B,C,D}, CorrectChoice, ExplanationCorrect, ExplanationWrong{A,B,C,D}, Difficulty, DifficultyScore, CognitiveLevel, CalculationItem, Type, LOSTag, BlueprintDomain, FormulaReference, CommonTrapReference, Authorities, VerificationChecks. No dual-block architecture.
conditions.rationale: Single-object architecture is the primary structural defense against DL-016 (metadata-content mismatch) and DL-029 (CC-offset false positives). Breaking this pattern would reintroduce P1 governance debt.
conditions.verification: Each Wave 2 item is one JSON object containing all fields. No paired metadata+content blocks. CorrectChoice and ExplanationWrong fields extracted from same object boundary.

conditions.condition: Wave 2 item topics SHOULD include foundational ratio definitions and straightforward calculations suitable for Remember/Understand/Apply cognitive levels. Defer complex multi-signal analysis and evaluative tradeoff items to Wave 3+.
conditions.rationale: Wave 1 items are sophisticated multi-layer business cases requiring Analyze/Evaluate judgment. Wave 2 needs items that test basic ratio computation (P/E, dividend yield, basic EPS, ROE), term matching (marketable securities classification, operating vs. finance lease identification), and single-step ratio interpretation without multi-signal integration.
suggestedTopics: Basic liquidity ratio computation (current ratio, quick ratio, cash ratio — single company, no industry comparison)
Activity ratio definitions (inventory turnover, DSO, DPO, total asset turnover — identify the correct formula)
Profitability ratio recall (gross margin, operating margin, net margin — definition match)
Basic DuPont identification (which ratios compose ROE/ROA decomposition)
EPS basics (basic vs. diluted, what goes in numerator/denominator)
Market value ratios (P/E, dividend yield, book value per share — straightforward computation)
Common-size financial statements (vertical analysis — identify the appropriate base)
Comparative analysis basics (horizontal analysis — year-over-year change computation)
Cash flow ratio basics (operating cash flow ratio definition, not multi-signal divergence)
Credit analysis fundamentals (single covenant evaluation, not multi-covenant tradeoffs)

risks.description: Wave 2 could compound difficulty/cognitive skew. If authoring behavior defaults to complex multi-layer scenarios (the Wave 1 pattern), Wave 2 will produce 30 more Difficult+/Analyze+ items, making the cumulative 60-item pool 100% Difficult+/Analyze+. This would require 90+ lower-tier items in Wave 3 just to begin approaching distribution targets. The 500-item pool target of 75 Easy items would become mathematically unreachable without massive corrective authoring.
risks.mitigation: Condition C01, C02, C06. Wave 2 must be explicitly focused on lower-tier items. Authoring should begin from the topic list in C06, not from complex business scenarios.

risks.description: Governance guard not registered as OpenCode plugin. Without write-time enforcement, a Wave 2 item could be saved with DL-008, DL-026, DL-021, or DL-037 defects. These would not be detected until the next programmatic validation run. The guard is functional (30/30 PASS) but requires manual invocation.
risks.mitigation: Condition C04. Every item validated through GovernanceGuardP2.validateItem() before save. Batch validation after all 30 items via validatePack().

risks.description: No governance guard test suite. If the guard module is modified or extended, there is no automated verification that all 11 rules still function correctly. A regression in Rule 2 (DL-008) or Rule 11 (Part2OnlyFlag) could go undetected across multiple authoring waves.
risks.mitigation: Prerequisite PR04. Test suite should be created before or early in Wave 2 authoring.

risks.description: Difficulty inflation (DL-031 pattern). Wave 1's authoring process produced items at Difficult+ and Analyze+ by default. The same authoring behavior, even when intentionally targeting lower levels, may produce items that are still too complex for their assigned labels. Definition-match items labeled Moderate when they test only Remember/Understand.
risks.mitigation: Condition C06 (explicit topic list). Each Wave 2 item's difficulty must be justified by cognitive demand, not by defaulting to the Wave 1 pattern. Apply-items should require exactly one computational step with formula substitution. Remember-items should be straightforward term-definition matches.

risks.description: P2-A-017 not fixed before Wave 2. If Wave 2 begins authoring while a known-broken item exists in the pack file, the unremediated defect could be forgotten or the item accidentally certified.
risks.mitigation: Prerequisite PR01 is BLOCKING. P2-A-017 must be fixed before Wave 2. The item should not remain in a broken state across authoring sessions.

risks.description: Batch size violation (Rule 5). If Wave 2's 30 items are written in a single change-set without BLOCK-AUTHORIZED marker, the governance guard will BLOCK the write.
risks.mitigation: Ensure the change-set includes BLOCK-AUTHORIZED marker or split into batches of ≤30 items. Since Wave 2 is exactly 30 items, a single batch with BLOCK-AUTHORIZED is compliant.

recommendations.description: Execute P2003_GOVERNANCE_BOOTSTRAP prerequisites M01-M14. The 14 mandatory items include: governance guard forking, test suite creation, pack file skeletons, REVISION_HISTORY_P2.md, DEFECT_LIBRARY_P2.md, CURRENT_BASELINES_P2.md, CAQS_P2_v1.0.md, FORMULA_MASTER_P2.md, ExplanationValidator_P2, build_master_registry_p2.js, AGENTS.md, CONSTITUTION, TAXONOMY_REGISTRY_P2.md, EXAM_BLUEPRINT_P2.md. P2 has taken a 'content first, infrastructure later' approach — Wave 1 produced 30 items before any of these existed. The technical debt from this sequencing is manageable for now but will compound with each wave.
recommendations.priority: Before Wave 3 authoring (can be deferred during Wave 2 if PR04-PR05 are completed)

recommendations.description: Register governance-guard-p2.js in opencode.json. Currently the plugin array lists only 'governance-guard' (P1). Adding a P2 guard entry would enable write-time enforcement and eliminate the manual validation requirement (Condition C04). The guard is designed as a standalone module — it needs an OpenCode plugin wrapper that calls it on file writes matching pack_p2_*.js.

Create an authoring template document (AUTHORING_TEMPLATE_P2.md) that codifies the Wave 1 structural pattern. The informal template is proven effective (30/30 clean items) but is not documented. A formal template would: (a) ensure consistency across future authors, (b) include difficulty/cognitive calibration guidance, (c) include the governance guard validation command, (d) list the required metadata field schema.

Establish baseline hashes for CURRENT_BASELINES_P2.md §5. Before Wave 2 begins (or immediately after P2-A-017 is fixed), compute SHA-256 hashes for pack_p2_a.js, governance-guard-p2.js, and all knowledge/foundation files. This enables T0 hash verification per the session startup protocol and drift detection during long sessions.

Run GovernanceGuardP2.validatePack('pack_p2_a.js') both before and after Wave 2 authoring. Pre-authoring run confirms baseline (expected: 30 items, 0 violations). Post-authoring run confirms Wave 2 items are structurally clean (expected: 60 items, 0 violations). This provides a verifiable governance gate that Wave 2 did not introduce structural defects.

Easy_1.note: Definition-match items: basic ratio definitions, term matching, formula identification. These are the easiest items to author and the most needed.

ModerateEasy_2.note: Single-step computations with clear inputs. Apply-level calculations that require substituting given numbers into a stated formula.

Moderate_3.note: Two-step computations or single-concept interpretation. May require selecting the appropriate formula from 2-3 candidates.

Difficult_4.note: Only if essential. Must not exceed 3 items. These should be the upper bound of Wave 2 complexity.

VeryDifficult_5.note: NONE. Wave 1 already has 9. Adding more would increase the cumulative Very-Difficult share beyond target.

Remember.note: Term-definition matching, ratio formula identification, authority citation recall. Straightforward single-choice items.

Understand.note: Explain what a ratio measures, interpret a computed ratio against a benchmark, classify a ratio as liquidity/solvency/profitability.

Apply.note: Compute a single ratio from given data, perform one DuPont decomposition step, calculate common-size percentages. Apply → single calculation path using a stated formula.

Analyze.note: Only the highest-quality items. Pattern should be: compute ratio + interpret against ONE benchmark (industry, prior year, or covenant). NOT multi-signal integration.

Evaluate.note: NONE. Wave 1 already has 14 Evaluate items (46.7% of the pool). The Domain A target is only 5% (25 items out of 500). Cumulative 14/500 (2.8%) is actually below target — but Wave 3+ should fill the remaining 11 Evaluate slots, not Wave 2.

recommended_topics: P/E ratio computation (EPS given, market price given)
Dividend yield and dividend payout ratio
Book value per share (basic, no preferred stock complications)
Basic vs. diluted EPS — identify which securities are dilutive
Gross margin percentage — compute from revenue and COGS
Operating margin — identify operating vs. non-operating items
Common-size balance sheet (express each line as % of total assets)
Common-size income statement (express each line as % of revenue)
Horizontal/trend analysis (year-over-year % change for a single line item)
Current ratio — what does a ratio of X mean for liquidity?
Quick ratio — why does it exclude inventory? (conceptual understanding)
Inventory turnover — identify from given COGS and inventory balances
Days sales outstanding — compute from given AR and sales
Cash conversion cycle — identify the three components
Debt-to-equity — what does a ratio >1.0 signal about capital structure?
Times interest earned — interpret a ratio <1.0
ROA basic decomposition — identify which two ratios multiply to ROA
ROE DuPont — identify the three components (NPM, TAT, EM)
Sustainable growth rate — identify the formula (no calculation required for Remember)
Operating cash flow ratio — what does it measure that current ratio cannot?
Free cash flow — identify from operating CF minus capex (conceptual)
Limitations of ratio analysis — which statements describe valid concerns? (Understand)
Segment reporting — why is disaggregated data important for ratio analysis? (Understand)
ASC 205 vs. ASC 842 — which standard governs which ratio analysis context? (Remember)
Classification of ratios — liquidity vs. solvency vs. profitability vs. activity (Remember/Understand)
prohibited_patterns: NO multi-signal integration (e.g., comparing current ratio, quick ratio, debt-to-equity, and operating cash flow simultaneously — Wave 1 pattern)
NO multi-year trend projection requiring compound growth rate calculation
NO strategic recommendation items (e.g., 'which capital structure should the company adopt?')
NO items requiring the candidate to reconcile conflicting ratio signals
NO items with >3 numerical calculations required to reach the answer
NO items where the correct answer depends on professional judgment rather than a single correct computational or definitional answer

B.note: Do NOT add more B-correct items. Current 12 (40%) already above ceiling. Cumulative: 12/60 = 20.0%. Let A/C/D catch up.

authoring_sequence.description: Term-definition matches and formula identification. Establish the Remember tier.
Conceptual understanding items. What does a ratio mean? Why exclude inventory from quick ratio? Classify ratios by type.
Single-step ratio computation with formula substitution. The Apply tier — the 45% target for Domain A.
Reserved for high-quality two-signal analysis. Only 3 slots — use judiciously. Compute + interpret against one benchmark.
